mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the certificate of incorporation and articles of the foreign corporate parent/incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry of the parent's jurisdiction as certified by that registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille jurisdictions, Consular Legalization at the nearest Canadian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of compliance of the corporate parent/incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry of the parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if required, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing a Quebec-based attorney-in-fact to execute incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document's jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the foreign notary is in an Apostille member state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for all directors, officers and individuals with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary or certificate of residence from the issuing government
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Notarized attestation with Consular Legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn beneficial ownership declaration (UBO statement) detailing the ownership structure and all qualifying individuals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Responsible officer or notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and, if foreign origin, authenticated by Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized representatives against the Government of Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council sanction list, and the Criminal Code's terrorism entity list under s. 83.05; positive matches trigger enhanced due diligence and possible Suspicious Transaction Reporting to FINTRAC. PEP/HIO protocols must conform to SOR/2002-184, ss. 50-53, requiring verification of the source of funds, regular monitoring, and senior management approval before onboarding. For any US-dollar payment rails or US-linked business, OFAC's SDN List and US Specially Designated Global Terrorist screening are also applied.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire d'entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) – online services portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11, s. 31) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, the corporate designation must be in French. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the French alphabet. A bilingual or English version may be accepted only if the French version is the legally recognized company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is refused, the Registrar issues a written refusal with statutory reasons. The applicant may correct and resubmit the name request online, or file an administrative review request with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar within 30 days, followed by an appeal to the Court of Québec as permitted by the Business Corporations Act and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if the registered office is a physical, staffed address in Quebec, accessible during business hours and capable of receiving service of process. Pure virtual or remote locations without an agent will not satisfy the commercial substance requirements for a regulated-substance professional consulting office. A licensed corporate service provider can supply a compliant registered office for this low-risk activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 15% over a 3-year horizon; on-site verification is typically triggered by tax anomalies, third-party complaints, or financial intelligence red flags rather than routine regulatory inspection for a non-licensed consulting firm.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended, ss. 8, 19, 49-52, 106-109; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 1-38
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for federal incorporation; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) for extra-provincial registration and legal publicity
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001 under the CBCA) filed through the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre; followed by the Initial Declaration (déclaration initiale) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA or QBCA; the corporation may be incorporated with one or more no-par-value common shares. No escrow or capital deposit account is required by the Registrar; subscription funds remain freely available as working capital in a Canadian bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscription of the incorporator be accepted and the subscribed shares issued fully paid as recorded in the share register. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at [address], Province of Quebec, and the Secretary file the required declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each holding office until successors are appointed. RESOLVED, that the officers be authorized to open bank accounts and complete all filings necessary for the Corporation's business. CERTIFIED as a true copy of the minutes of the first directors' meeting on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre in coordination with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec name research service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request through the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) protocol to obtain a search report confirming the proposed name is distinguishable and not confusing. For extra-provincial registration in Quebec, verify that the corporate name complies with the French-language rules of the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) for the registered office and establishment name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (with French form if registering in Quebec)
Primary business purpose and NAICS 541690 description
Full names and residential addresses of proposed directors
Canadian legal representative designation where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name request or a change of name under CBCA s. 173 without repeating the incorporation; Corporations Canada provides a reasoned refusal notice and permits a limited number of resubmissions under the original application fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) - Online Filing Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 with the approved corporate name, registered office address in Canada, share structure (classes, rights, restrictions), and number of directors. Submit electronically, pay the filing fee, and receive the electronic Certificate of Incorporation in PDF format.
required_dossiers: Form 4001 Articles of Incorporation
NUANS name search report
Director consent forms and declarations
Registered office address and share provisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada rejects the articles for incomplete or non-compliant provisions, correct the deficiencies and resubmit in the same online session; the Director may issue corrective instructions under CBCA s. 251 for technical irregularities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors after issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. Adopt the pro forma First Board Resolution confirming the share subscription, fixing the registered office, appointing officers, and authorizing bank and regulatory filings. Record and execute minutes in the corporate records book.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
First Board Resolution (pro forma text)
Share subscription ledger and allotment schedule
Consent of officers to act
Minutes of the organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed director is disqualified or an officer declines appointment, the remaining directors may appoint replacements by majority resolution at the same meeting; amend the minutes and update the share and officer registers accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-Provincial Registration and Initial Declaration in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Initial Declaration (déclaration initiale) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 60 days of obtaining the federal Certificate of Incorporation. Indicate the Quebec establishment address, legal form, officers, and federal business number. Pay the statutory fee and publish the registration in the public register.
required_dossiers: Initial Declaration form (Déclaration initiale)
Federal Certificate of Incorporation
Quebec establishment address proof
Business Number (BN) issued by the CRA
Names and addresses of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the declaration (e.g., missing French name, address, or officer information), amend and refile within the prescribed correction window to avoid late-filing penalties under s. 100 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec for provincial accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain the 9-digit Business Number and register for the GST/HST account (mandatory once annual taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000), payroll deductions, and corporate income tax account T2. Register separately with Revenu Québec for QST, employer health contribution, and provincial payroll deductions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
First Board Resolution appointing financial officers
Business address and establishment address in Quebec
Directors' personal identification and residency information
Banking confirmation from the corporate account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec rejects the registration or assigns an incorrect account status, contact the Business Enquiries line or Revenu Québec's business services to submit corrective filings; maintain the T2 corporate and GST/HST accounts through CRA My Business Account portals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Payment Rails Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I chartered bank in Canada and corporate officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate operating and wire-transfer bank account presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, certified first board resolution, and officer identification. Establish an anti-money-laundering (AML) compliant banking profile for the regulatory consulting business and activate the target payment rails: Bank Wire and Credit Card through an approved payment processor.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Quebec extra-provincial registration receipt
Certified First Board Resolution appointing signatory officers
Passport or government identification for each signing officer
Corporate address confirmation (lease or utility bill in Quebec)
Beneficial ownership declaration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank invokes enhanced due diligence for non-resident officers or the beneficial-ownership declaration, provide source-of-funds evidence and updated corporate records to complete KYC; the bank must provide written reasons for any account refusal, after which the corporation may file a complaint with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no sectoral industrial permit is triggered for an office-based ISIC 7490 regulatory consulting business. If a physical laboratory, quality-testing facility, or manufacturing site is later established, Health Canada's Medical Devices Bureau under the Food and Drugs Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-27, and, for industrial establishments, the Quebec Société du bâtiment (SBQ) / CNESST would apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Professional-services operating permit not required under Quebec law for regulatory consulting; the only compulsory formalities are the business establishment declaration to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and, for medical device advice, compliance with the general professional and contractual obligations applicable to consultants.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction générale de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - administrative consulting office activities are not listed in the mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment schedule of the Règlement relatif à l'évaluation des impacts sur l'environnement, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 23.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or air emission sources exist for the consulting activity. Any office fit-out must comply with municipal wastewater and waste by-laws (e.g., Ville de Montréal by-laws); waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) must be handled under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises, CQLR c. E-2, r. 23.1; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions remain below the de minimis occupational threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance certificate issued by the competent local fire safety authority (e.g., Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal or the municipal fire service) confirming the leased office meets the Quebec Construction Code and National Fire Code; workplace health and safety clearance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c. S-2.1, with a CNESST prevention program; structural load inspection is required only if a mezzanine, record vault, or heavy storage equipment is installed in the leased premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) — federal Business Number/GST/HST registration, filing, and collection; portal: Business Registration Online and CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/account.html). Quebec-specific: Revenu Québec — QST, employer payroll contributions, and sectoral tax credits; portal: Mon Dossier d'entreprise (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or foreign-incorporated entity must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA using Business Registration Online or Form RC1. The BN is the statutory TIN for direct tax and is the parent number for program accounts: GST/HST (14-character number, e.g., RT000000001), payroll deductions (RP), and import/export (RM). The application requires certified constitutional documents, proof of foreign incorporation, board authorization appointing a Canadian representative or agent, and a Canadian service/mailing address. After the BN is granted, the same entity must register with Revenu Québec for QST using Form LM-1 or the online QST registration service, and must obtain a Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) establishment number whenever it maintains an establishment in Quebec. Registration obligations are mandatory before taxable activities begin unless the small-supplier threshold applies; a non-resident with a Quebec permanent establishment cannot claim the small-supplier threshold for QST if its gross revenue from that establishment exceeds CAD $30,000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A federal/provincial business corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a separate legal taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act; there is no pass-through or check-the-box classification in Canada. Profits, losses, assets, and liabilities are taxed at the corporate level, with integration achieved through eligible dividend rules. A US/foreign LLC or similar hybrid entity is not recognized as a Canadian corporation unless incorporated in Canada; foreign limited-liability status is assessed under CRA's foreign entity classification rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election. Relevant elections include: (1) allocation of taxable income among associated corporations under ITA s.256; (2) non-resident's s.216 election to compute tax on rental/royalty income on a net basis; (3) rollover elections under ITA ss.85, 86, and 88 for incorporation, reorganization, and amalgamation; (4) GST/HST nil-consideration relief elections between closely related corporations under ETA ss.156-157 and the corresponding QST election; (5) deemed dividend and surplus elections for transactions with foreign affiliates; and (6) hybrid mismatch rules in Part XVI.1 of the ITA operate as anti-abuse disgorgements, not elective regimes. Foreign entity classification is determined by legal form and CRA administrative rules; there is no elective check-the-box mechanism for Canadian tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST). Quebec is a non-harmonized province: the federal GST applies at 5%; Quebec applies QST at 9.975%, yielding a combined consumer-facing tax rate of 14.975% (before applicable provincial rebates).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST and QST, the general small-supplier threshold is CAD $30,000 of total worldwide taxable revenues from taxable supplies in the preceding four calendar quarters (increasing to CAD $50,000 for charities). A non-resident carrying on a taxable business in Canada, including through a Quebec permanent establishment, is required to register regardless of Canadian revenues if the permanent establishment generates taxable sales; remote sellers and digital marketplace operators must register once Canadian taxable sales exceed CAD $30,000 on a 12-month basis. In Quebec, the same CAD $30,000 threshold triggers QST enrollment for non-residents, except that a permanent establishment in Quebec may create a mandatory registration even below that threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or integrated e-invoice validation exists for GST/QST in Canada. Quebec operates a self-assessment VAT system: a supplier must issue an invoice in paper or electronic format containing prescribed identifiers (supplier's name and address, CRA BN and QST number, date, description of supply, consideration, and GST/QST rates and amounts). The Pan-Canadian and Quebec public-sector e-invoicing frameworks are being implemented on a voluntary/B2G basis, not as a tax clearance precondition. CRA and Revenu Québec may require taxpayers to provide fiscal records in digital format on audit, and electronic sales suppression is prohibited. There is no API pre-clearance gateway for issuing merchant receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are zero-rated under GST/HST Schedule VI Part V and corresponding QST rules when the supplier exports the goods, transfers them to an authorized carrier/consignee for export, or exports them within prescribed time limits, and retains documentary proof of export. Regulatory consulting services for FDA 510(k) filings and CE marking supplied by a Quebec corporation to a foreign client are zero-rated as taxable supplies made to a non-resident where the recipient is a non-resident and the service is not received in Canada (not in respect of real property located in Canada, not performed for goods situated in Canada, and not an exempt supply). If the consultant conducts inspections or work physically in Quebec, the portion performed inside Canada may be taxable unless the supply is otherwise zero-rated as an export service in respect of software/intellectual property located outside Canada or in respect of the client's foreign business. Services supplied entirely to a non-resident for use outside Canada and not connected to Canadian real or tangible property should be zero-rated, allowing input tax credit recovery on related expenses.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A, CAED, or CBSA-compliant customs export record) for physical goods; for services-only contracts, a service export declaration/attestation setting out the offshore nature of the work
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or international carrier receipt showing the goods left Canada; for services, signed delivery/service completion certificate with the foreign client's foreign address
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT/MT103 credit advice, or bank statement evidencing foreign currency proceeds received into a Canadian financial institution
Executed client agreement identifying the foreign purchaser, jurisdiction, regulatory scope (FDA/CE), and place of use or benefit

Non-resident status confirmation obtained from the client (e.g., client's foreign TIN/VAT number or certificate of registration in the destination country) and, where applicable, overseas customs entry or regulatory submission reference
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec can reassess a taxpayer to recover uncollected GST/QST plus arrears interest and, in cases of misrepresentation, extend the normal four-year assessment period to seven years. Claiming zero-rating without sufficient export evidence triggers denial of refunds, reversal of input tax credits, and penalties: late or incomplete filings attract 5% plus 1% per month (possibly 10%/12% for repeated failures); false statements or omissions can draw penalties of CAD $250 to CAD $25,000 under the Excise Tax Act and comparable Quebec penalties; gross negligence penalties equal 25% of the misreported net tax; fraud or evasion can result in criminal fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years. Exporters are expected to create and retain a contemporaneous export evidence file for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acts as the monetary and macroprudential authority, but Canada does not operate an exchange-control administration. The policy levers for restrictions are held by the Minister of Finance under the Investment Canada Act and by Global Affairs Canada under sanctions and export-control legislation; FINTRAC supervises cross-border transaction reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). A corporate treasury in Quebec therefore deals with the Bank of Canada only indirectly, through payments systems and settlement (Large-Value Transfer System) rather than FX licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction and provides full current-account and capital-account convertibility for CAD, USD, and EUR, without advance approvals, counterparty quotas, or conversion schedules. Profit remittance is unrestricted: a Quebec subsidiary may declare dividends at any time if the solvency test (Quebec Business Corporations Act) is met, and remittance is effected via any bank or FX provider. The only frictions are taxation: non-resident withholding under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (25% standard, reduced by treaty) and Quebec-specific income tax compliance for the paying corporation. Loans and intellectual-property royalties must be invoiced at arm's length to avoid recharacterization as deemed dividends under subsections 212(2) and 212(3) of the ITA, in addition to Part XIII royalty withholding rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, minimum retention period, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; all receipts may be held in CAD or foreign currency. The only regulatory filters are (i) FINTRAC's mandatory electronic funds transfer reporting threshold of CAD 10,000, which is executed by the clearing financial institution on the client's behalf, and (ii) CBSA/FINTRAC cross-border currency and monetary instruments declaration for physical cash or bearer instruments of CAD 10,000 or more. The Canadian parent entity may therefore deliver a USD/EUR cross-currency blend into Quebec operations without central-bank pre-clearance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD) + USD and EUR multi-currency clearing sub-accounts; optional Capital Escrow Trust Account for client milestone funds
Operating Account (CAD) + RBC U.S. Business Account (USD, ABA/Fedwire clearing)
Operating Account (CAD) + BMO U.S. Dollar Account with BMO Harris Bank correspondent clearing
Operating Account (CAD) + TD U.S. Dollar Business Account with U.S. clearing rail
Operating Account (CAD) + CIBC U.S. Dollar Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low-to-Medium, structurally subordinate to a Schedule I bank account. Offshore electronic-money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer are not licensed to open deposit accounts in Quebec; they operate as foreign money transfer businesses and must, if soliciting Canadian clients, be registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC under PCMLTFA. Wise Business's Canadian implementation is provided through a licensed MSB partner and can be used only as a tactical disbursement rail for small EUR/USD payments to European notified bodies or FDA-tool vendors. The primary operating account, credit line, and reserve balances must remain at a Canadian Schedule I bank; unrestricted foreign EMIs are deemed a compliance weakness in KYC and FX audit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec-incorporated business corporation, Schedule I banks require at least one director or senior signing officer to complete a face-to-face interview (branch in Montreal or any Quebec commercial centre) or a live, bank-managed video interview with dual-process identity verification. Full remote opening is available for low-risk models using PCMLTFA section 60(2) attestation via a Canadian financial institution or notary, but any foreign beneficial owner is almost certain to trigger an in-person/video interview and a request for certified passport and proof of address. Documents in a language other than French must be accompanied by a certified translation (Charter of the French Language); apostilles issued after Canada's accession to the Hague Apostille Convention (effective 11 January 2024) are accepted, though pre-convention legalization from the Ministère de la Justice du Québec may be required for dated records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or remote-only beneficial owners (25% or more voting control) with no Canadian nexus, typical in an international MedTech consulting founder ledger.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed UBO register and Declaring Director certificate; notarized passports and proof of residential address; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; sanctions screening clearance against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List; written description of the founder's functional role in Quebec operations; no third-party transaction authority on the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office setup and low tangible physical presence (the firm renders services online to U.S./EU clients).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease in Quebec (bail commercial) for 24+ months; payroll evidence for Quebec employees/consultants (R-1 RL slips / Revenu Québec remittances); corporate income-tax returns (TPI) and financial statements; client contracts evidencing substantive performance of FDA/CE consulting work from Canada; company operations documentation if requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High credit-card inbound volume from foreign clients (target rail is Card), which can trigger merchant acquirer concerns over refund/chargeback abuse or concealment of professional fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS certification of card-processing stack; standing A/R invoicing set with matching credit-card settlement reports; chargeback-and-refund policy document; prohibition of third-party card use; historical sales/purchase orders and engagement letters; merchant agreement with Moneris or Worldpay configured for cross-border settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injections arriving as large one-shot wires from a foreign bank into a newly opened account, presenting a layering/reverse-payment red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription resolution and board approval minute; securities register and share issuance ledger; parent/shareholder source-of-funds documentation from the remitting bank; SWIFT MT103 copies; statement that no cash or crypto was used; undertaking that further injections will be designated EQUI/INTC in the wire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Founder/shareholder capital must be remitted as a SWIFT MT103 (or MT101 in batch) to a Quebec Schedule I beneficiary, e.g., National Bank of Canada (SWIFT BNDCCAMMONT). The wire must identify the purpose code EQUI (Equity) or INTC (Intra-Company Payment); no Canadian pre-clearance is required, and no replacement of foreign exchange takes place unless a conversion is requested. The financial institution will file the mandatory FINTRAC EFT report when the amount equals or exceeds CAD 10,000. The treasury must retain the share subscription resolution, the Quebec securities register, and an FX conversion statement if the injection is in USD/EUR. Target revenue rail (credit-card) is integrated through the merchant acquirer on the same operating account: card settlements arrive in CAD or USD with 1-3 day value dating and are reconciled to A/R by invoice number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: U.S. FDA 510(k) user fees are paid through the USD-denominated clearing sub-account (ABA/Fedwire rail) rather than a cross-border international wire, avoiding correspondent fees; EU notified-body fees are paid via SEPA Credit Transfer from an EUR sub-account (or SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA banks). General outbound vendor payments engage SWIFT MT103/MT101; urgent Canadian-dollar disbursements use the Large-Value Transfer System (LVTS) and low-value payroll/purchases use Interac or standard EFT. For prototype/ancillary equipment imports, a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) or Standby LC may be issued against the operating account, supported by the bank's trade-services line. Corporate card disbursements require a documented expense policy, merchant categorization, and monthly card-to-supplier audit. All outbound payments must reference the underlying commercial invoice and, where relevant, the FDA PMA/510(k) or CE technical-file number for regulatory fee traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot (T+2 settlement) for CAD/USD/EUR receivable conversion
Outright Deliverable FX Forward, tenor up to 24 months, executed under a bank Master FX Agreement with exposure netting
FX Swap (spot-plus-forward combination) for precise liquidity-date management
Vanilla FX options (call/put, including zero-premium collar structure) for cost-effective premium-free hedging
Cross-currency swap (CAD/USD or USD/EUR) only where an audited multi-year financial liability exists, under ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) are NOT permissible for CAD/USD/EUR because convertibility is unrestricted; NDFs are outside treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) - Corporations Canada Form 22; official filing fee CAD 12 online / CAD 40 paper
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; deadline is not linked to fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee CAD 100; failure to file for 1 full year permits the Director of Corporations Canada to publish a notice of default in the Canada Gazette, followed by administrative dissolution of the corporation; revival possible on payment of all arrears and penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Updating Declaration (Declaration de mise a jour annuelle) filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; official online fee CAD 33
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the company's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; applies to both Quebec-incorporated and extra-provincial corporations carrying on business in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty CAD 58; after repeated non-filing (generally two consecutive missed annual declarations) the Registraire may initiate strike-off and dissolution proceedings after publishing a preliminary notice in the Gazette officielle du Quebec; on dissolution, corporate property may escheat to the State

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax returns - federal T2 return to the Canada Revenue Agency and Quebec CO-17 return to Revenu Quebec; no government filing fee applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; tax balance-due day is the same deadline; the company fiscal year typically ends on December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delay, up to 12 months (federal and Quebec); repeated failure may be prosecuted as a summary offence; directors may incur personal liability for unremitted source deductions and GST/QST under subsection 227.1 of the Income Tax Act and Quebec fiscal legislation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based audit threshold for a private non-distributing CBCA or Quebec Business Corporations Act company; a mandatory independent audit applies only to distributing (public) corporations. A private consulting corporation may waive the annual audit by unanimous shareholder consent at the annual meeting; if waived, a review engagement or compilation is commonly substituted by lenders or investors.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE - CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private corporations in Quebec and federally; both frameworks are accepted for T2 and CO-17 reporting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the CBCA Register of Individuals with Significant Control (RISC) and the Quebec register des personnes ayant un controle important (RPACI), the corporation must take reasonable steps at least once each fiscal year to identify individuals holding 25% or more of voting shares, any control in fact, or contractual control rights. Share transfers and UBO changes must be recorded in the register within the prescribed update window (15 days for director changes and promptly for UBO changes), and the annual federal return and Quebec annual updating declaration confirm the currency of the register. A director who knowingly fails to maintain the register may be prosecuted; a federal offence can attract a fine of up to CAD 5,000 and/or imprisonment, with comparable Quebec administrative penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders ledger with share allotments and transfers)
Minute Book (board and shareholder meeting minutes and unanimous resolutions)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (CBCA RISC / Quebec RPACI)
Register of Share Transfers and Security Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 300-700 (approx. USD 225-525) per year for registered office address and corporate agent/secretarial services in Quebec; no statutory professional licence premium applies to this MedTech regulatory consulting entity since it holds no regulated healthcare licence.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 8,000-25,000 (approx. USD 6,000-18,500) for a full independent audit of a small private consulting corporation; reduced to CAD 4,000-8,000 (approx. USD 3,000-6,000) for a review engagement where the audit is waived by unanimous shareholder consent.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec provincial 11.5% (general rate) = 26.5% combined; small business rate reduced to 9% federal and 3.2% provincial on first CAD 500,000 active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits; Quebec Innovation tax credits; patent box regime (federal and provincial) for qualifying IP income; manufacturing and processing profits deduction (federal 13% on eligible income)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via CRA's NETFILE/EFILE portal; Quebec: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via Revenu Québec's e-services
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after fiscal year-end for both federal and Quebec returns; tax payments due in quarterly installments based on prior-year or current-year estimates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross worldwide revenue; allocate to Canada based on permanent establishment rules
Adjust for Canadian tax purposes; include only Canadian-source income if treaty applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions and loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply non-resident withholding tax provisions; claim treaty relief if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed calculation of taxable income and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach transfer pricing documentation if transactions with non-residents exceed thresholds

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeated failure: 10% plus 2% per month; daily interest on unpaid amounts (CRA prescribed rate, currently 8% for 2025); Quebec similar penalties under Taxation Act

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross dividends paid to non-residents (Part XIII tax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (Form NR301 for Canada) to the payer; the payer must file Form NR601 (or equivalent) with CRA to apply the treaty rate; for Quebec, additional provincial withholding may apply but is generally reduced under treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties and interest; treaty rates typically 10% for royalties (e.g., US) and 15% for interest (or 0% for arm's length interest under US treaty); Quebec imposes an additional 12% withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents, but treaty relief may reduce this

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for goods; CAD 500,000 for services; CAD 250,000 for intangibles (per transaction or aggregate with non-arm's length non-residents)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions require genuine economic substance; a shell company without real activity may be denied treaty benefits and subject to reassessment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or misrepresentation of transfer pricing to reduce taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239: fine up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties: 50% gross negligence penalty on understated tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes (s.227.1) if they failed to withhold or remit; travel bans and asset freezes possible under criminal proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporation without real business activity, no employees, no physical presence, or artificial intercompany arrangements to shift profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment (s.245) denying tax benefits; treaty shopping denial under OECD BEPS; penalties up to 10% of tax avoided; potential criminal charges for fraudulent misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in sham arrangements; travel bans and extradition risk in cross-border cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a money services business (MSB) if providing payment services; failure to report suspicious transactions or maintain compliance under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for individuals and CAD 2,000,000 for corporations; criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned if they knowingly fail to implement AML policies; travel bans and seizure of assets possible
